notes: Legs went far better than push did on the same sleep debt — "super tired but did pretty good." **The kneeling leg curl landed and he wants to keep it**: found 50 → 60 → 65 on the first run and described it as *"preacher curls for legs."* The two spotlights both did their job — the curl gave the isolation the seated machine used to, and the reworked incline RDL turned from a stamina lift into a discipline lift exactly as intended. Both squat and leg press produced a good read on the same theme: control through the descent, and warmth deciding how the first set feels. He ran the day in his own order (curl and RDL before the leg press) and closed with a program-direction question about rotating implements. He labelled it `w27d3`; it was Wednesday, day 2, legs.

exercises.notes: Three working sets at 80, all clean, **and he left power on the table on purpose** — *"three sets with power left but decided to hold off."* The depth assignment produced the sharpest self-report yet: *"feeling like i'm getting a good feel of my power band as i go down lower and how much power i'm losing, and i'm working on getting lower and lower and maintaining control and power band."* That is the loaded bottom being mapped rather than avoided — W26 banked stability, this week banked awareness of where power falls off in the descent.

Ran **left side first** and **12 reps on every set, both sides.** Load found by climbing: 50 → 60 → 65, with 60 already *"a struggle."* **The asymmetry showed up: *"right side is way easier lol."*** Same load both sides by design — the number was found on the left, so the right doing it comfortably is the protocol working, and the first time the left-side lag has been measured in the lower body.
